papers.abstract: Whether an action-conditioned world model uses actions is usually checked by replacing or removing them and measuring lost accuracy. With biological experiments as the guiding case, we show that such diagnostics report action effects where there are none: under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history the model does not see, and a better model learns the stand-in better. When the design law is known, a conditional randomization test written as an e-value is valid in finite samples whatever the model, provided the resampler conditions on the full state the design used; resampling from a simpler law reproduces the false effect. A second failure is specific to world models: when many sites share one action sequence (cells in a microscope field, pixels in a frame), the pooled score turns small model errors along the action contrast into overwhelming evidence against a true effect. In a pixel world, its median log e-value fell from $-17.3$ to $-6832$ as frames grew from 64 to 4096 pixels, while the oracle's rose. Our preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed this way; a tempered statistic, selected on synthetic data and registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field ($E\approx1.1\times10^{10}$). Tempering factors estimated from residuals can err by an order of magnitude, whereas a mixture over a fixed grid of factors needs no estimate and loses at most the logarithm of the grid size in log e-value relative to its best member. In a registered test on a diffusion world model for three Atari games released by others, the pooled test rejected in 0 of 96 units in which actions mattered and Kish and contrast tempering in 0 and 1, while the mixture rejected in 96; under an exact null, eight statistics made 0 rejections in 1,536 tests. Every analysis is preregistered, fixed in a dated protocol, or labelled exploratory.

analysis.key_results: 在像素世界中，随着帧从64增至4096像素，中位对数e值从-17.3降至-6832；混合方法在96个动作相关单元中全部拒绝，而池化检验在0个单元中拒绝；在精确零假设下1,536次检验零拒绝。
analysis.limitations: 回火因子估计可能误差一个数量级；混合方法需要固定网格；实验限于生物和特定游戏世界模型。
analysis.main_contribution: 识别并解释了动作条件世界模型中两种系统性失败：自相关设计下未来动作成为历史替身，以及池化评分放大微小模型误差导致假阳性；并提出基于e值和混合回火的解决方案。
analysis.method: 条件随机化检验（e值）与混合回火统计量，并使用像素世界和Atari扩散世界模型进行验证。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文借鉴生物实验设计，揭示了动作条件世界模型中动作效应检验的两种失败模式，并提出了有效的统计检验方法。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 研究世界模型中动作效应的检验可靠性，对动作条件世界模型（WAM）的评估方法有直接价值，但不涉及视觉-语言-动作（VLA）或机器人操作。

papers.abstract: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research.

analysis.key_results: 在跨所有模态的综合嵌入基准上建立了新的 Pareto 前沿，超越了专家模型以及大 2 到 12 倍的模型。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 EmbeddingGemma 2，一种统一的多模态嵌入模型，并引入模型量化等效率优化特性。
analysis.method: 简化每层嵌入、多阶段课程学习（模态与目标递进）、选择性模态编码器加载、可调视觉 token 预算、截断嵌入维度和量化权重。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出了一种开源多模态嵌入模型，统一表示文本、图像、音频、视频及其组合，并在性能和效率上取得新突破。

papers.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can perceive a traffic scene, reason about it, and propose a driving action within a single model. However, existing MLLM-based drivers reason from scratch at each frame and commit to a single explanation, discarding earlier hypotheses about the scene. When the scene is ambiguous, the agent locks in on the wrong interpretation and acts on it before evidence accumulates. In this paper, we propose DriveMind, an MLLM-based driving framework that keeps several hypotheses about the scene alive at the same time and updates their weights as new frames arrive. Inspired by particle filtering, DriveMind propagates each hypothesis through a VLM, scores it against the current observation, and resamples to maintain diversity. On Bench2Drive, adding belief tracking to the same driving pipeline improves the Driving Score (DS) from 68.50 to 81.37 and the Success Rate (SR) from 41.36% to 54.09%. The largest gains occur on ambiguous scenarios such as unsignalized intersections (+20.0 DS) and oncoming-traffic interactions (+20.5 DS). Beyond the overall metrics, DriveMind also improves fine-grained interactive driving abilities such as merging, emergency braking, and give-way.

analysis.key_results: 在 Bench2Drive 上，加入信念跟踪使 Driving Score 从 68.50 提升至 81.37，Success Rate 从 41.36% 提升至 54.09%，在无信号交叉口和迎面车流等模糊场景增益最大。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出一种基于 MLLM 的驾驶框架 DriveMind，通过维持多个场景假设并按新帧更新权重，解决了现有 MLLM 驾驶模型在模糊场景中过早锁定单一解释的问题。
analysis.method: 受粒子滤波启发，DriveMind 将每个假设通过 VLM 传播，根据当前观测打分并重采样以保持多样性，从而维持并更新多个场景信念。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: DriveMind 提出了一种基于多模态大语言模型的自动驾驶框架，通过粒子滤波式的多假设信念跟踪，在闭环驾驶中持续更新场景解释并提升驾驶性能。

papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) jointly predict robot actions and future observations, but their video diffusion backbones are costly for edge deployment. We introduce SmolWAM, a compact latent WAM derived from the 2B-parameter Cosmos Policy using single-frame encoding, cached text features with preserved attention sinks, depth pruning, and token compaction. With 12 of 28 transformer blocks and 1,008 tokens, SmolWAM predicts actions and future latents in one rectified-flow step. After 3.6 A100 GPU-hours of training, it achieves 95.5% success over 400 LIBERO episodes at 57ms, 2.3TFLOP, and 2.4GiB per 16-action chunk on an A100: 11x lower latency and 3.2x lower memory than the five-step teacher. Its world head predicts scene motion; joint training improves success by 6.2 percentage points over an action-only ablation.

analysis.key_results: 在400个LIBERO回合上达到95.5%成功率；每16个动作块在A100上延迟57ms、计算量2.3TFLOP、内存2.4GiB；延迟比五步教师模型低11倍，内存低3.2倍；联合训练比仅动作分支高6.2个百分点成功率。
analysis.main_contribution: 从2B参数的Cosmos Policy中压缩得到一个紧凑的潜在世界-动作模型，通过单帧编码、缓存文本特征、保留注意力汇聚、深度剪枝和令牌压缩，实现高效的机器人操作。
analysis.method: 单帧编码、缓存文本特征与注意力汇聚、深度剪枝、令牌压缩、整流流一步预测。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出SmolWAM，一个从2B参数Cosmos Policy压缩得到的紧凑潜在世界-动作模型，在保持高成功率的同时显著降低推理延迟和内存占用。

papers.abstract: Monocular 3D object detection spans two regimes: closed-set detectors operating within a fixed category vocabulary, and open-vocabulary detectors that localize arbitrary categories by leveraging depth foundation models for 3D geometry. We find that current depth foundation models, despite their strong zero-shot generalization, lack the object-level precision 3D detection demands: substituting a state-of-the-art depth foundation model for a strong detector's predicted depth degrades accuracy. Rather than pushing detectors or depth models to be more accurate end-to-end, we treat object-level depth refinement as a stand-alone task and present RefineAny3D, a vision-language model that corrects depth without ever predicting a numerical value. Our key insight is that depth error has a direct visual signature in image space: when projected onto the image, a correctly placed box tightly encloses the object, while a too-far box projects too small and a too-close box projects too large. Depth refinement thus reduces to a visual alignment problem rather than a metric regression problem, which we instantiate by extending the VLM's vocabulary with action tokens that replace numerical depth output with categorical decisions, and by supervising the model on a large-scale chain-of-thought dataset that grounds each decision in explicit visual evidence. Applied as a single post-hoc step, RefineAny3D delivers consistent gains across closed-set detectors, open-vocabulary detectors, and 3D auto-labeling tools, and generalizes to novel categories, scenes, and cameras without retraining. Code is available at https://github.com/alanzhangcs/RefineAny3D.

analysis.key_results: 应用于封闭集检测器、开放词汇检测器和3D自动标注工具时，均取得一致的性能提升，并泛化到新类别、场景和相机而无需重新训练。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出RefineAny3D，将目标级深度细化作为独立任务，用视觉语言模型进行分类决策而非数值回归，并通过动作token和链式思维数据集实现无需重新训练即可泛化到新类别、场景和相机。
analysis.method: 将深度误差转化为图像投影框与目标的对齐问题，扩展VLM词汇表以动作token替代数值输出，并在大规模链式思维数据集上监督训练。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: RefineAny3D是一种视觉语言模型，通过将深度细化转化为图像空间中的视觉对齐任务来纠正单目3D检测中的目标深度误差。

papers.abstract: We present FlowPilot, the first world-action model for real-time onboard UAV navigation from depth. Unlike map-then-optimize pipelines that require local reconstruction or end-to-end policies that lack explicit scene prediction, FlowPilot jointly denoises future depth observations and executable trajectories with flow matching. A dual-stream mixture-of-transformers couples video and action experts through shared attention, allowing future-scene prediction and trajectory generation to inform each other. At deployment, the model runs action-centrically and outputs only a trajectory. To generate smooth, state-consistent references, actions are parameterized as degree-7 Bernstein polynomials: the current state constrains the initial control points, and the network predicts five free control points, yielding C^2-continuous references with closed-form velocity, acceleration and jerk. FlowPilot is trained on a three-level depth pyramid spanning high-throughput simulation, photorealistic simulation, and real onboard data. In closed-loop simulation, it outperforms learning- and optimization-based baselines under increasing clutter and commanded speeds up to 10 m/s. On a physical quadrotor, FlowPilot achieves a mean inference latency of 10.2 ms on a Jetson Orin NX and reaches a peak speed of 10 m/s during outdoor flight using only onboard sensing and computation.

analysis.key_results: 在封闭环路仿真中，FlowPilot 在不断增加的环境杂乱度和最高 10 m/s 指令速度下优于基于学习和基于优化的基线；在实际四旋翼上，Jetson Orin NX 上平均推理延迟为 10.2 ms，户外飞行达到 10 m/s 峰值速度。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 FlowPilot，第一个用于无人机实时机载导航的世界-动作模型，能够在深度观测和轨迹之间进行联合预测，并在实际四旋翼上以 10.2 ms 延迟和 10 m/s 峰值速度运行。
analysis.method: 采用双流混合专家 Transformer，通过共享注意力耦合视频和动作专家，并使用流匹配联合去噪未来深度和轨迹；动作以 7 阶 Bernstein 多项式参数化，约束初始控制点并预测五个自由控制点，生成 C^2 连续参考轨迹。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: FlowPilot 是一个通过流匹配联合去噪未来深度观测和可执行轨迹的世界-动作模型，在机载边缘设备上实现了实时敏捷无人机导航。

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation; however, their transition to real-world environments reveals vulnerabilities to minor environmental perturbations. We propose FLARE, an optimization framework that exploits these vulnerabilities via targeted illuminations, causing critical disruption of baseline tasks. While adversarial training is the standard countermeasure, we identify a critical and previously underestimated defensive pitfall: naive data augmentations condition VLA models to largely discard color as noise, biasing their visual perception toward shape cues. We expose this degradation through a diagnostic grayscale evaluation, in which a naively defended model maintains high success rates on grayscale inputs, while its success rate on benign, color-dependent real-world tasks drops to at most 48.8%, compared with 78.8% for the undefended SmolVLA baseline. To address this, we propose ChromaGuard, a chroma-preserving adversarial training method. On a physical 6-DoF robotic platform using SmolVLA, we demonstrate that ChromaGuard achieves 95.0% and 88.8% success rates in benign and attacked color-dependent tasks, respectively. Demo videos are available at https://keio-csg.github.io/ChromaGuard/.

analysis.key_results: 在物理6-DoF机器人平台上，ChromaGuard在良性和攻击的颜色依赖任务中分别达到95.0%和88.8%成功率，而朴素防御模型在良性任务中成功率最多48.8%，未防御SmolVLA为78.8%。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出ChromaGuard，一种保持色度的对抗训练方法，解决VLA模型在光照攻击下因朴素数据增强而丧失颜色感知的问题，并在真实机器人上验证了其有效性。
analysis.method: FLARE攻击框架利用目标照明制造关键扰动；ChromaGuard为色度保持的对抗训练，通过诊断性灰度评估揭示颜色线索丢失问题。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 针对VLA模型在照明扰动下的脆弱性，提出攻击框架FLARE和防御方法ChromaGuard，以保留颜色线索并提升鲁棒性。

papers.abstract: Exploration is essential to reinforcement learning (RL) since a policy cannot improve by repeatedly sampling the behaviors it already prefers. Standard methods inject stochasticity in the action space, but such jitter only yields rollouts close to the original action distribution. Escaping a weak policy often requires global perturbations that action noise cannot produce. Large language models (LLMs) and vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a pathway: they condition the policy on a natural language prompt, and since the rollout follows from it, modifying the prompt induces global changes. The challenge is finding prompts that induce useful global changes. With a weak policy that rarely succeeds, reward is too sparse to select on. Our idea is to refine prompts from the rollouts themselves: a vision-language model (VLM) reasons over the rollout video, diagnoses how the policy responded, and rewrites the prompt to elicit better behavior next time. Sampling a prompt and holding it fixed throughout a rollout provides episode-level commitment, analogous to posterior-sampling exploration. We call this strategy Prompt Driven Exploration (PDE). Across manipulation and reasoning tasks, PDE enables RL to learn successful policies even from zero-reward starts, and improves sample efficiency more broadly. Our website is available at https://xinyunsunshine.github.io/prompt-rl.

analysis.key_results: 在操作和推理任务中，PDE使强化学习即使在零奖励起始状态下也能学到成功策略，并更广泛地提高了样本效率。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出Prompt Driven Exploration (PDE)方法，利用VLM对rollout视频进行推理并改写语言提示，将语言作为全局探索空间，使VLA策略能从零奖励初始状态学到成功策略。
analysis.method: 在每次rollout中采样一个语言提示并保持固定，通过VLM观察回放视频诊断策略行为，并重写提示以引导后续探索，实现近似后验采样的探索策略。

papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) deploy into mission-critical domains (e.g., finance, medicine, and law), output reproducibility has become a strict system requirement. While practitioners use greedy decoding to eliminate algorithmic stochasticity, empirical deployments with 16-bit precisions still exhibit catastrophic output divergence across heterogeneous GPUs. Through SASS-level profiling, we reveal that this inconsistency is fundamentally driven by truncation errors introduced during downcasting at kernel boundaries. However, achieving reproducibility via a global FP32 pipeline incurs prohibitive system penalties: bypassing 16-bit hardware accelerators hurts compute efficiency, while upcasting the KV cache doubles memory overhead. To bridge this gap, we propose Hybrid Error ALleviation (HEAL), a targeted intervention that approximates FP32 precision while resolving hardware constraints through two targeted mechanisms. First, recognizing that floating-point formats underutilize their bit-width for Q, K, V tensors, HEAL applies INT16 quantization that preserves numerical stability without expanding the KV cache footprint. Second, HEAL synthesizes high-precision matrix multiplications via an algebraic error compensation strategy, executing entirely on high-throughput 16-bit Tensor Cores. To evaluate our approach practically, we introduce MCR-Bench, a benchmark targeting reproducibility in mission-critical tasks. HEAL achieves the same level of reproducibility on downstream tasks as the FP32 baseline while reducing the performance overhead by up to 6.0$\times$.

analysis.key_results: HEAL在下游任务上实现了与FP32基线相同的可复现性，同时性能开销降低了最多6倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出HEAL，一个在16位硬件加速器上实现FP32级可复现推理、同时大幅降低性能开销的针对性干预方法。
analysis.method: HEAL对Q、K、V张量应用INT16量化保持数值稳定性，并通过代数误差补偿在16位Tensor Core上合成高精度矩阵乘法。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出HEAL方法，通过INT16量化和代数误差补偿，在保持FP32级可复现性的同时，显著降低LLM推理的性能开销。

papers.abstract: We study how trajectory-shape diversity in demonstrations affects imitation learning (IL) performance across models, tasks, and data scales. We introduce Geometric Entropy (H_G), a task-agnostic metric that quantifies the intrinsic diversity of transit trajectories after normalizing away extrinsic variation, such as goal pose and workspace scale, via target-frame alignment. Across multiple IL architectures and both simulated and real-robot contact-rich manipulation tasks, we observe a consistent inverted-U relationship between success and H_G: increasing geometric diversity improves robustness in low-diversity regimes but degrades performance once diversity induces strategy ambiguity. Moreover, the optimal entropy shifts toward lower values as task mastery increases through more data, easier tasks, or stronger priors, and for a pretrained vision-language-action model the trend becomes effectively monotonic decreasing. Practically, H_G enables fast pre-training auditing of demonstration datasets and offers a simple guideline for calibrating demonstrations toward the learnable regime.

papers.abstract: Closed-loop driving simulators mostly fill their environments with traffic agents that behave alike, whether they are rule-based or learned. Recent methods that control driving style learn it from labels inferred from existing driving recordings, from synthetic data generated to reflect each style, or from reward weights estimated by a large language model (LLM). All of these are indirect estimates of a style, not recordings of people who were instructed to drive in it. We introduce PersonaDrive, a vision-language-action (VLA) driving agent that takes its style from retrieved human demonstrations. The demonstrations come from a new dataset in which 15 participants drove CARLA routes on a driving simulator under conservative, neutral, and aggressive instructions. PersonaDrive trains a lightweight retrieval head on features from a frozen image encoder and on control signals over per-style databases, and fine-tunes one VLA backbone over the retrieved demonstrations. Switching style only means searching a different FAISS index, with no retraining. On the Bench2Drive benchmark without style conditioning, PersonaDrive improves the Driving Score by 4.6% over SimLingo and by 2.5% over HiP-AD, a gain that fine-tuning without retrieval does not reproduce. With style conditioning, PersonaDrive outperforms the strongest baseline, Drive My Way, in every style, with a Driving Score 6.7% to 11.6% higher. Its driving also follows the instruction, since average speed rises by 19.8% from the conservative to the aggressive style. Each traffic agent is evaluated individually as a driving policy. The dataset and model weights are available on the project page: https://pervasiveautonomylab.github.io/personadrive-landpage/.

analysis.key_results: 在无风格条件的Bench2Drive基准上，PersonaDrive的驾驶得分比SimLingo高4.6%，比HiP-AD高2.5%；在有风格条件时，每种风格下均优于最强基线Drive My Way，驾驶得分高出6.7%至11.6%，且平均速度从保守到激进风格提升19.8%。

analysis.method: 利用冻结图像编码器的特征和每类风格的数据库训练轻量级检索头，对检索到的演示微调一个VLA骨干网络；风格切换只需搜索不同的FAISS索引。

papers.abstract: Multisensory perception is essential for robotic manipulation, with tactile sensing providing critical information for fine-grained, contact-rich interactions. Although prior work integrates tactile and spatial signals to improve perception, vision-tactile learning commonly relies on object-level alignment. Addressing this limitation requires systematically aligned 3D vision-tactile data. We develop a data collection system and introduce Touch3D, a dataset comprising 505 real-world objects and 20,025 tactile contacts. Building on this dataset, we establish the Contact-Centric Multimodal Tactile Representation Benchmark (CoMT-Bench), which expands evaluation from object-level retrieval and tactile properties to include patch-level contact evaluation. We further propose Geometry-Relation Distilled Tactile-Centric Cross-Modal Learning (GeoTAC), which explores tactile learning across all multisensory data. In experiments on the Touch3D test set, patch-level alignment improves the average score by 5.32 over object-level alignment, with GeoTAC's geometric supervision improving it by a further 4.48. In robotic manipulation, GeoTAC improves TP by 19.14 and 11.34 over DINOv2 (Vision-only) and DINOv2 (Vision-Tactile), respectively. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/tacdino.

analysis.key_results: 在Touch3D测试集上，块级对齐比物体级对齐平均得分高5.32，GeoTAC的几何监督进一步提升4.48；在机器人操作中，GeoTAC的TP比DINOv2（仅视觉）高19.14，比DINOv2（视觉-触觉）高11.34。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出了Touch3D数据集（包含505个真实物体和20025个触觉接触）、CoMT-Bench评估基准，以及GeoTAC方法，探索了所有多感官数据的触觉学习。

papers.abstract: Learning high quality latent actions from large-scale unlabeled videos, coupled with limited real-world interaction data for training an action decoder, has emerged as a promising paradigm for scalable latent policy learning. However, existing approaches typically rely on behavior cloning, which tends to collapse inherently multimodal action distributions into unimodal ones, thereby degrading the pretrained latent action structure. While flow matching provides a potential alternative, directly applying it leads to a misalignment between latent actions and physical actions during action decoder training, due to the stochastic nature of the learned policy. To address these, we propose Latent Action Flow Policy (LAFP), which leverages flow matching for latent policy learning and introduces an inference-time interpolation mechanism to mitigate stochasticity-induced misalignment. Experimental results demonstrate that LAFP consistently outperforms prior methods on most downstream imitation learning tasks, achieving an 8.2\% improvement in average success rate while incurring less than 1x additional inference overhead.

analysis.key_results: 在大多数下游模仿学习任务上优于先前方法，平均成功率提升 8.2%，且额外推理开销小于 1 倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 Latent Action Flow Policy (LAFP)，利用流匹配学习潜在策略，并引入推理时插值机制以减轻随机性导致的潜在动作与物理动作之间的错位。
analysis.method: 使用流匹配进行潜在策略学习，并在推理时采用插值机制来缓解随机性引起的错位。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: LAFP 利用流匹配进行潜在策略学习，并通过推理时插值机制减轻随机性引起的错位，从而保持预训练潜在动作结构。

papers.abstract: Force and tactile sensing are essential for contact-rich manipulation, but their integration into handheld or wearable devices is constrained by cost, size, and mechanical compatibility. Tactile signals are also sensitive to manufacturing variations and wear during use, posing further challenges to policy learning. To address these hardware and learning challenges, we introduce AetheRock, an arm-worn device for collecting gripper-force, visual, and tactile data. AetheRock incorporates GelSlim-Mini, our improved version of GelSlim 4.0 designed for low-cost, easy manufacturing, at the gripper fingertip, together with a resistive pressure sensor at the human finger contact area. To learn robust representations from the collected data, we propose ForceVT, a framework that aligns multimodal representations and uses force and vision to guide tactile learning, mitigating the effects of manufacturing variations and sensor degradation. Real-world experiments demonstrate efficient data collection with AetheRock. ForceVT improves average performance by 13% over the vision-tactile baseline and maintains an average task progress of 55.0% under reduced tactile fidelity, compared with 58.0% at full fidelity. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/aetherock.

analysis.method: 利用GelSlim-Mini低成本触觉传感器和电阻式压力传感器采集抓取力、视觉和触觉数据；ForceVT对齐多模态表示并以力和视觉指导触觉学习。

papers.abstract: Mobile agents are increasingly expected to operate everyday applications from screenshots and language goals, where reliable control requires reasoning over screen affordances, multi-step navigation, and future state changes. However, many agents externalize this computation as long textual chains of thought, which slows interaction, increases supervision cost, and complicates deployment. We introduce MIRAGE, a framework that learns continuous latent reasoning representations from visible textual reasoning traces. MIRAGE transfers explicit reasoning into compact hidden states, enabling the agent to reason internally without decoding long rationales. It also incorporates a generative world-model objective: latent reasoning vectors are aligned with future screenshots, encouraging the agent to anticipate upcoming interface states before acting. This turns hidden computation into both a compressed thought representation and a forward-looking model of environment dynamics. At inference time, MIRAGE reasons in continuous latent space, reducing token generation while improving execution efficiency. On AndroidWorld, MIRAGE matches explicit chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning in the 4B ablation with a 3-5x lower decoded-token budget and improves a comparable instruction-tuned baseline by 10.2 points; on AndroidControl, it improves action grounding while generating over 75% fewer tokens.

papers.abstract: We study the query complexity of sampling from high-dimensional Gaussian distributions using gradient information. In the standard oracle model, exact gradients expose only matrix-vector products with the precision matrix, leading to polynomial approximation barriers and a characteristic $\sqrt{\kappa}$ dependence on the known spectral range. We show that this barrier disappears when the sampler is allowed to query smoothed scores, namely gradients of the logarithms of the Gaussian-convolved densities. For a centered Gaussian target with precision matrix $\Lambda$, a smoothed-score query at noise level $\tau$ gives access to the resolvent $(\Lambda+\tau^{-1}I)^{-1}$. Combining geometrically spaced noise levels with sinc-quadrature rational approximation, we obtain a sampler with $q=O((\log\kappa+\log(e\sqrt d/\delta_{\rm TV}))\log(e\sqrt d/\delta_{\rm TV}))$ smoothed-score queries for total variation error $\delta_{\rm TV}$, improving the condition-number dependence from $\sqrt{\kappa}$ to logarithmic. We also study finite-bit gradient oracles. Using coordinatewise quantization of the transformed smoothed-score answers and a final dithering step, we obtain a sampling scheme whose total communicated gradient information is polylogarithmic in $\kappa$; in particular, for fixed dimension and accuracy, the bit complexity is $O(\log^2\kappa)$. To complement these upper bounds, we introduce a channel-synthesis, or reverse-Shannon, converse technique for sampling lower bounds. This converts total-variation simulation guarantees into communication requirements and yields an $\Omega(d\log\kappa)$ bit lower bound for $d\ge2$ and fixed total variation error below one, as $\kappa\to\infty$. Together, these results identify smoothed scores as a provably more informative oracle for sampling and give nearly matching upper and lower bounds for its finite-bit complexity.

analysis.key_results: 查询复杂度从O(sqrt(kappa))改善至对数级，有限比特下比特复杂度为O(log^2 kappa)上界和Ω(d log kappa)下界。

papers.abstract: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models and world action models (WAMs) advance robotic manipulation by enriching intermediate representations with auxiliary spatial features or future visual-state prediction. However, these representations largely remain within the observation space and do not share the rigid-body geometry of the action space, forcing the action decoder to implicitly recover this geometry. We propose OASIS, a visuomotor policy that aligns the intermediate representation with the action space via $SE(3)$ end-effector trajectory prediction. OASIS couples a 3D-aware feature encoder that fuses vision-language and metric-depth features with an $SE(3)$ trajectory predictor that produces a camera-frame end-effector trajectory. Conditioned on the predictor's pose-supervised hidden states, the action decoder generates action chunks consistent with rigid-body motion. Across simulation and real-world experiments, OASIS outperforms VLA and WAM baselines in success rate and out-of-distribution generalization. Our project page is available at https://oasis-neurips.github.io.

papers.abstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions. Building on an offline-learned bottleneck policy interface introduced by previous work, ZPRL turns this representation into an online RL control space through reward-driven residual perturbations while freezing the pretrained policy. We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Videos and code can be found at https://manutdmoon.github.io/ZPRL/.

papers.abstract: Many inference-time language-model pipelines combine a cheap reward signal with an expensive verifier, such as exact answer checking in mathematical reasoning or hidden-test execution in code generation. We formalize this setting using a learning-theoretic lens as generative active search: a cost-sensitive first-positive search problem in which a policy adaptively samples candidates from an unknown distribution, observes cheap scores, and pays for verifier labels until it finds a positive example. For a fixed prompt, the generator and reward model induce two unknown objects: a distribution over reward scores and a score-conditioned success function. When these quantities are known, we characterize the distribution-aware optimal policy using a dynamic programming approach. In the realistic and practical setting where both the score distribution and success function are unknown, we propose ADAP, a shellwise adaptive generate-rank-verify algorithm that progressively increases the number of sampled responses and top-ranked verifications. Under the monotonicity assumption that higher reward scores are no less likely to pass verification, we show that ADAP achieves expected cost within a constant factor of the distribution-aware optimum. We complement this result with learning-theoretic lower bounds, based on a centered star number, showing that structural assumptions on the score--label relationship are necessary. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and competitive programming validate the predicted advantage over both fixed non-adaptive policies and difficulty-adaptive baselines.

papers.abstract: Test-time model evolution offers a promising way for deployed models to improve from unlabeled test-time experience, yet most existing methods depend on backpropagation (BP), which incurs substantial memory overhead and makes them difficult to deploy on edge devices, quantized models, specialized accelerators, or black-box models. In this work, we study test-time model evolution under a strict two-forward budget, a setting that pushes adaptation toward highly efficient real-world deployment. We reveal three key obstacles in zeroth-order test-time optimization: susceptibility to shortcut solutions, uncontrolled weight drift, and ineffective update direction estimation. To overcome them, we propose EVA-0, a minimal zeroth-order adaptation framework that: 1) keeps the loss scale-invariant to prevent shortcut solutions; 2) devises an anchor-guided optimization strategy to alleviate weight drift; 3) uses sample-wise symmetric two-sided perturbation for update direction estimation and inference. EVA-0 requires no BP and performs both inference and adaptation within only two forward passes per sample. Results on ImageNet-C & ViT-Base show that EVA-0 outperforms both BP-based DeYO and BP-free FOA, while achieving a 14x speed-up over FOA. Code will be released.

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models remain constrained by the scarcity of action-labeled robot data, whereas action-free videos provide abundant evidence of how the physical world changes. Latent action models offer a promising way to extract such priors from videos, but reconstruction-trained latent codes are not necessarily suitable for policy generation: they may predict future observations while lacking the structure needed to be reused or generated coherently with robot actions. We introduce ALAM (Algebraic Latent Action Model), an Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model that turns temporal relations in action-free video into structural supervision. Given frame triplets, ALAM learns latent transitions that are grounded by reconstruction while being regularized by composition and reversal consistency, encouraging a locally additive transition space. For downstream VLA learning, we freeze the pretrained encoder and use its latent transition sequences as auxiliary generative targets, co-generated with robot actions under a joint flow-matching objective. This couples structured latent transitions with flow-based policy generation, allowing the policy to exploit ALAM's locally consistent transition geometry without requiring latent-to-action decoding. Representation probes show that ALAM reduces additivity and reversibility errors by 25-85 times over unstructured latent-action baselines and improves long-horizon cumulative reconstruction. When transferred to VLA policies, ALAM raises the average success rate from 47.9% to 85.0% on MetaWorld MT50 and from 94.2% to 98.1% on LIBERO, with consistent gains on real-world manipulation tasks. Ablations further confirm that the strongest improvements arise from the synergy between algebraically structured latent transitions and joint flow matching. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Mark-zjtang/ALAM/tree/main.

papers.abstract: World models for deformable objects should recover not only geometry and appearance, but also underlying physical dynamics, interaction grounding, and material behavior. Learning such a model from real videos is challenging because deformable linear, planar, and volumetric objects evolve under high-dimensional deformation, noisy interactions, and complex material response. The model must infer a physical state from visual observations, roll it forward under new interactions, and render the resulting dynamics with high visual fidelity. We therefore present DeformMaster, a video-derived interactive physics-neural world model that turns real interaction videos into an online interactive model of deformable objects within a unified dynamics-and-appearance framework. DeformMaster preserves structured physical rollout while using a neural residual to compensate for unmodeled effects, grounds sparse hand motion as distributed compliant actuators for hand-continuum interaction, represents material response with spatially varying constitutive experts, and drives high-fidelity 4D appearance from the predicted physical evolution. Experiments on real-world deformable-object sequences demonstrate DeformMaster's ability to roll out future dynamics and render dynamic appearance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while supporting novel action rollout, material-parameter variation, and dynamic novel-view synthesis. Code and video demos are available at the project page: https://can-lee.github.io/deformmaster-web/

papers.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance across vision tasks, yet their deployment with low-precision early exiting remains fragile. Existing quantization methods assume static full-depth execution, making them unstable when exit decisions are perturbed by quantization noise, which can amplify errors along dynamic inference paths. In this paper, we introduce Amortized-Precision Quantization (APQ), a utilization-aware formulation that accounts for layer utilization when modeling quantization error and reveals depth-precision trade-offs. Building on APQ, we propose Mutual Adaptive Quantization with Early Exiting (MAQEE), a bi-level framework that jointly optimizes exit thresholds and bit-widths under explicit risk control to improve inference stability. MAQEE establishes a superior Pareto frontier in the accuracy-efficiency trade-off across classification, detection, and segmentation, with comparisons at predefined task-specific performance targets. On ImageNet, it achieves 79.41% Top-1 accuracy while reducing BOPs by 10.9% relative to utilization-only allocation. Measurements of the deployed models on an RTX 5090 show GPU throughput improvements of $2.26\times$ on ImageNet and $3.06\times$ on CIFAR-100 over full-depth FP32 inference. Source code is available at https://github.com/Rui-Fang/MAQEE.

analysis.key_results: 在ImageNet上达到79.41% Top-1准确率，同时相比仅利用率的分配减少10.9% BOPs；在RTX 5090上相比全深度FP32推理，ImageNet吞吐量提升2.26倍，CIFAR-100提升3.06倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出Amortized-Precision Quantization (APQ)，一种考虑层利用率的量化误差建模方法，并进一步提出Mutual Adaptive Quantization with Early Exiting (MAQEE)，联合优化退出阈值和位宽，在显式风险控制下改善推理稳定性，并在精度-效率权衡上取得更优的Pareto前沿。

papers.abstract: A prevailing view in robot learning is that simulation alone is not enough; effective sim-to-real transfer is widely believed to require at least some real-world data collection or task-specific fine-tuning to bridge the gap between simulated and physical environments. We challenge that assumption. With sufficiently large-scale and diverse simulated synthetic training data, we show that zero-shot transfer to the real world is not only possible, but effective for both static and mobile manipulation. We introduce MolmoBot-Engine, a fully open-source pipeline for procedural data generation across robots, tasks, and diverse simulated environments in MolmoSpaces. With it, we release MolmoBot-Data, a dataset of 1.7 million expert trajectories for articulated object manipulation and pick-and-place tasks. We train three policy classes: MolmoBot, a Molmo2-based multi-frame vision-language model with a flow-matching action head; MolmoBot-Pi0, which replicates the $\pi_0$ architecture to enable direct comparison; and MolmoBot-SPOC, a lightweight policy suitable for edge deployment and amenable to RL fine-tuning. We evaluate on two robotic platforms: the Franka FR3 for tabletop manipulation tasks and the Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 mobile manipulator for door opening, drawer manipulation, cabinet interaction, and mobile pick-and-place. Without any real-world fine-tuning, our policies achieve zero-shot transfer to unseen objects and environments. On tabletop pick-and-place, MolmoBot achieves a success rate of 79.2% in real world evaluations across 4 settings, outperforming $\pi_{0.5}$ at 39.2%. Our results demonstrate that procedural environment generation combined with diverse articulated assets can produce robust manipulation policies that generalize broadly to the real world. papers.abstract: Inference efficiency in Large Language Models (LLMs) is fundamentally limited by their serial, autoregressive generation, especially as reasoning becomes a key capability and response sequences grow longer. Speculative decoding (SD) offers a powerful solution, providing significant speed-ups through its lightweight drafting and parallel verification mechanism. While existing work has nearly saturated improvements in draft effectiveness and efficiency, this paper advances SD from a new yet critical perspective: the verification cost. We propose TriSpec, a novel ternary SD framework that, at its core, introduces a lightweight proxy to significantly reduce computational cost by approving easily verifiable draft sequences and engaging the full target model only when encountering uncertain tokens. TriSpec can be integrated with state-of-the-art SD methods like EAGLE-3 to further reduce verification costs, achieving greater acceleration. Extensive experiments on the Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen/LLaMA families show that TriSpec achieves up to 35% speedup over standard SD, with up to 50% fewer target model invocations while maintaining comparable accuracy.

papers.abstract: Correction notice (v2). Two implementation issues affect these experiments. All LoRA training ran under DeepSpeed, which replaced the optimizer passed to the Trainer with AdamW at a constant learning rate, so the Muon and Adam arms used the same optimizer. The cross-entropy term was computed without the next-token shift, so the preference for alpha = 1 reflects that objective rather than the value of the teacher. Each comparison also uses a single GPTQ quantization, and repeated quantizations differ by up to several points. The findings on Muon's quantization robustness, the distillation weight and accuracy relative to GPTQ alone should not be relied on. See the notice on page 1. Large Language Models (LLMs) enable advanced natural language processing but face deployment challenges on resource-constrained edge devices due to high computational, memory, and energy demands. Optimizing these models requires addressing three key challenges: acquiring task-specific data, fine-tuning for performance, and compressing models to accelerate inference while reducing resource demands. We propose an integrated framework combining GPTQ-based quantization, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), and a specialized data distillation process to significantly reduce model size and complexity while preserving or enhancing task-specific performance. By leveraging data distillation, knowledge distillation via Kullback-Leibler divergence, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, and the Muon optimizer, our pipeline achieves up to 2x memory compression (e.g., reducing a 6GB model to 3GB) and enables efficient inference for specialized tasks. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance on standard LLM benchmarks compared to GPTQ quantization alone, with the Muon optimizer notably enhancing fine-tuned models' resistance to accuracy decay during quantization.

analysis.key_results: 实现高达2倍内存压缩（例如将6GB模型减少到3GB），并在标准LLM基准上优于单独使用GPTQ量化，Muon优化器增强了微调模型对量化精度衰减的抵抗能力。
analysis.limitations: 摘要本身未说明局限；但版本2修正通知指出LoRA训练使用了恒定学习率、交叉熵计算缺少next-token shift、单一GPTQ量化导致重复量化结果差异大，因此有关Muon量化鲁棒性、蒸馏权重和相对GPTQ的精度结论不可靠。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出结合GPTQ量化、LoRA、数据蒸馏、知识蒸馏、贝叶斯超参数优化和Muon优化器的集成框架，实现高达2倍内存压缩并提升特定任务性能。
analysis.method: 使用GPTQ量化、低秩适应（LoRA）、数据蒸馏、KL散度知识蒸馏、贝叶斯超参数优化和Muon优化器。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出一种结合GPTQ量化、LoRA低秩适应、数据蒸馏和Muon优化器的集成框架，用于减少LLM在边缘设备上的部署资源需求。

papers.abstract: We introduce OpenMarkX, an extensible platform for watermarking open-source model and agent outputs under standard inference. It takes models, compatible methods, private keys, and evaluation settings, and produces watermarked weights, detection results, and quality and robustness reports. Its 16 text-watermark configurations are complemented by agent, vision-language, image, and physics-field workflows. Our proposed method, OpenMark, addresses learnability and robustness through joint model--policy learning and perturbation-aware training. On several open-source LLMs, OpenMark achieves 0.92 TPR at 1% FPR while reducing perplexity by 20.5% on average relative to the strongest prior method, and remains more detectable after such modifications, e.g., retaining 0.57 TPR at 5% FPR after 0.5-ratio model merging, compared with at most 0.34 for prior methods.

papers.abstract: In wireless communication systems, efficient and adaptive resource allocation is essential for enhancing overall Quality of Service (QoS). Compared with conventional Model-Free Reinforcement Learning (MFRL), Model-Based RL (MBRL) first learns a generative world model for subsequent planning, enabling more stable training through the reuse of historical experience. However, deploying MBRL in large-scale wireless networks remains challenging due to high-dimensional stochastic dynamics, strong inter-agent cooperation, and stringent communication constraints. To overcome these challenges, we propose a Multi-Agent Conditional Diffusion Model Planner (MA-CDMP) for decentralized communication resource management. Following the Decentralized Training with Decentralized Execution (DTDE) paradigm, MA-CDMP models each communication node as an autonomous agent and employs Diffusion Models (DMs) to capture environment dynamics. An inverse dynamics model is further incorporated to guide action generation, improving sample efficiency and policy scalability. Moreover, to efficiently approximate large-scale agent interactions, we introduce a Mean Field (MF) mechanism to assist the classifier in conditional DMs. This mitigates inter-agent non-stationarity and enhances cooperation with minimal communication overhead. We further establish an upper bound on the distributional approximation error induced by MF-based diffusion generation, guaranteeing convergence stability and reliable modeling of multi-agent stochastic dynamics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MA-CDMP consistently outperforms existing MARL baselines in terms of average reward and QoS metrics, showcasing its scalability and practicality for real-world wireless network optimization.

papers.abstract: Vision-Language Model (VLM) driving agents promise explainable end-to-end autonomy by first producing natural-language reasoning and then predicting trajectory planning. However, whether planning is causally driven by this reasoning remains a critical but unverified assumption. To investigate this, we build DriveMind, a large-scale driving Visual Question Answering corpus with plan-aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT), automatically generated from nuPlan. Our data generation process converts sensors and annotations into structured inputs and, crucially, separates priors from to-be-reasoned signals, enabling clean information ablations. Using DriveMind, we train representative VLM agents with Supervised Fine-Tuning and Group Relative Policy Optimization and evaluate them with nuPlan's metrics. Our results, unfortunately, indicate a consistent causal disconnect in reasoning-planning: removing ego/navigation priors causes large drops in planning scores, whereas removing CoT produces only minor changes. Attention analysis further shows that planning primarily focuses on priors rather than the CoT. Based on this evidence, we propose the Reasoning-Planning Decoupling Hypothesis, positing that the training-yielded reasoning is an ancillary byproduct rather than a causal mediator. To enable efficient diagnosis, we introduce a novel, training-free probe that measures an agent's reliance on priors by evaluating its planning robustness against minor input perturbations. In summary, we provide the community with a new dataset and a diagnostic tool to evaluate the causal fidelity of future models.
